_comment: A PC takes two floppy drives with independent swap lists, a CD-ROM, and up
to two hard disks. Following the DOSBox-X core: the hard disk slot's file
SEEDS a writable image rather than being written in place, and what comes
back out is the whole disk, byte for byte, so it can be handed straight
back into this slot to carry on from.
There is deliberately no slot for a PCem .cfg: the machine is composed from
settings, and letting a user paste in a config would reintroduce exactly the

slots.title: Floppy disks (drive A:)
slots.help: Images for drive A:. The first is in the drive at boot; the order here is the swap order. The drive itself is the Floppy Drive A setting, which defaults to Auto and fits the drive to whatever image you put here. If you set a drive by hand, mind that it matches: PCem does not refuse a disk the drive cannot reach, it clamps the head at the drive's last track and the guest gets read errors instead.

slots.title: Floppy disks (drive B:)
slots.help: Images for drive B:, the same way. A machine with only one drive ignores this.

slots.title: CD-ROMs
slots.help: Discs for the CD-ROM drive. PCem reads the image itself, so a .cue with its tracks beside it works. Needs a machine with a CD-ROM controller - the CD-ROM settings appear once there is a disc here.

slots.title: Hard disk (C:)
slots.help: A hard disk image, mounted as drive C:. It seeds a writable disk rather than being written in place: writes persist for the session, travel in savestates, and can be exported as save data - and an exported image can be given back here to continue from. Geometry is derived from the file unless the Hard Disk settings say otherwise.

slots.title: Second hard disk (D:)
slots.help: A second hard disk, the same way.
